items.stem:
Read the passage below, based on the play 'On the Face of It', and answer.

"BOY: You don't stare at my arm.
OLD WOMAN: (still shelling peas) Why would I? It's an arm. I've got a crooked back. Do you stare at that?
BOY: (pause) No.
OLD WOMAN: Well, then. Pass me that bowl. These peas won't shell themselves.
BOY: (smiling for the first time) No, I suppose they won't."

Answer the following:
(i) What does the boy notice about the old woman?
(ii) What is the old woman's own disability?  (a) Blindness  (b) A crooked back  (c) A burnt face  (d) A tin leg
(iii) What theme of "On the Face of It" does this extract share?
(iv) What is the tone of the old woman's speech?  (a) Matter-of-fact and warm  (b) Angry  (c) Fearful  (d) Mocking
items.answer: (i) She does not stare at his arm. (ii) (b) A crooked back (iii) Acceptance of disability and friendship that heals loneliness. (iv) (a) Matter-of-fact and warm
items.markingKey: (i) She does not stare at his arm. (ii) (b) A crooked back (iii) Acceptance of disability and friendship that heals loneliness. (iv) (a) Matter-of-fact and warm (1 mark each, 4 marks.)
